title: Sleep Not, Soldier of the Cross
description: Sleep Not, Soldier of the Cross in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 314, “Sleep Not As Do Others”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sleep not, sol-dier of the cross! Foes are lurk-ing all a-round; Look not here to find re-pose, This is but thy bat-tle ground.

lines: Sleep not, soldier of the cross!
Look not here to find repose,
Up! and take thy shield and sword;
Up! it is the call of Heaven;
Shrink not faithless from thy Lord,
Nobly strive as he hath striven.
Break through all the force of ill;
Tread the might of passion down;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
